messages:
OpsBot: :rotating_light: ALERT at 18:40 UTC — kv-cache eviction pressure high on gpupool-prod-4, paging started, latency spike 4–6x for text-generation routes. Auto-scaled workers are hitting OOMs. Logs attached: `kv_size_bytes=1.8GB -> 6.4GB in 7m`
Priya: ack — I'm looking. rough idea? any recent rollouts?
Marc: saw a canary earlier today that switched gptq->awq quant path for the Llama-3 family at 18:10. Could be related.
Jess: confirm: continuous-batcher config was bumped to batch_timeout=30ms and max_batch_tokens=4096 in that rollout. Might exacerbate KV retention.
Arjun: quick check of node metrics: page-in rate spike correlates with inflight KV cache growth on single worker type. Kernel selection logs show fallbacks to int8 kernels at long seq lengths.
Priya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause AWQ rollout across prod, 2) set continuous-batcher.max_batch_tokens=2048 and batch_timeout=10ms via feature-flag, 3) force kv_cache.eviction_threshold=0.6 on affected pools. Who can flip flags?
Marc: I can patch the FF now — doing feature flag rollback for quant-path (awq->gptq fallback) for Llama-3-global. Pushing change.
OpsBot: Feature flag change applied by Marc at 18:47 UTC.
Priya: reduce batch size on routing rule for text-gen routes to 1 for customers with >5% latency increase — target the largest tenants first. Marc/Lina-CS will coordinate.
Lina-CS: I have customer list and alerted top 3 affected customers (acme-inc, bookify, docflow) via high-priority tickets. We're noting degraded latency but no loss of completions for now.
Jess: rolling restart needed for workers to reclaim huge KV mem? We should avoid full pool restart unless necessary. Suggest applying kernel-selection override to prefer fp16 kernels for now: `kernel.select_override = "prefer_fp16"` — that will force non-int8 path and reduce per-KV footprint. Arjun: can we do that without restart?
Arjun: kernel override is hot-pluggable in runtime v2.8.2 — can apply on the fly to nodes with that runtime. I'm running a canary apply on two nodes now.
Priya: runbook step: apply to canary, monitor kv_size and paging. If it drops and latencies improve, roll to remaining nodes with 5-min pause between batches. Jess/Arjun coordinate.
Marc: can we also enable temporary aggressive KV eviction policy: `kv_cache.max_entries=50000` on the pool to force eviction of inactive prefixes? I'll stage the change.
OpsBot: Marc scheduled kv_cache.max_entries override at 18:52 UTC.
Arjun: canary results: kv_size on node-a dropped from 5.9GB -> 1.9GB in 90s after kernel override + eviction. Paging IO rate normalized. Latency returned to ~1.2x baseline.
Priya: good. initiate bulk rollout to remaining nodes in gpupool-prod-4 with 5-min stagger. Marc/Jess start.
Jess: rollout in progress — applying kernel override + eviction + batch limits. rolling restart skipped.
Lina-CS: customers updated: acme-inc seeing <10% request errors, 40% queued requests during peak at 18:42–18:50, now degraded latency only. Creating incident tickets INC-2149/INC-2150.
Marc: also reverted continuous-batcher.timeout bump and reduced max batch tokens via FF. OpsBot confirms flag: continuous-batcher.batch_timeout=10ms, max_batch_tokens=2048.
OpsBot: Flag change confirmed at 19:03 UTC.
Arjun: note: root cause hypothesis — awq quant path produced larger per-token KV representations for certain attention layers (observed ~2.8x KV footprint vs gptq) combined with longer effective sequence lengths from batching change, which pushed working set beyond GPU memory and triggered paging. Kernel selection fallback to int8 path also chose a kernel variant that maintained larger KV blocks.
Priya: Customer impact summary (so far) — 6 customers had elevated tail latency; 2 had transient 5xx spikes (acme-inc and bookify) during the peak window 18:40–18:50. No data loss; logs show single in-flight truncation for a handful of long-running streams. CS notified.
Lina-CS: Sent customers post-incident notes and currently setting expectation for follow-up 1:1s.
Jess: temporary mitigation status: kernel override + eviction + batch limits applied across gpupool-prod-4 at 19:07 UTC. Observed stable metrics for 15m.
Marc: I've also queued a scheduled capacity bump of 2x ephemeral workers for gpupool-prod-4 in case of another surge — will keep it paused unless needed.
Arjun: action items for next 24h: 1) revert AWQ rollout cluster-wide after postmortem or recreate AWQ with KV size cap, 2) add automated regression test measuring KV footprint for quant paths using long-seq synthetic prompts, 3) add runtime metric for per-model kv_entry_size histogram, 4) refine kernel-selection logic to avoid int8 path for models with heavy KV allocations.
Priya: oncall handoff to night shift @Marc at 20:00 UTC. Marc, you're primary; Jess backup. Please keep the rollout paused and monitor gpupool-prod-4.
Marc: ack handoff — monitoring dashboards pinned. If paging >3x or kv_size growth resumes, enable capacity bump and revert to FP16 model variant.
OpsBot: Handoff note recorded: incident-1803750000 assigned to Marc at 20:00 UTC.
Priya: tagging for postmortem: owners = Arjun (root cause / infra), Jess (runtime ops), Marc (deploy/feature flags), Lina-CS (customer comms). We'll schedule postmortem tomorrow 14:00 UTC.
Lina-CS: I'll gather customer impact summaries and example request IDs for postmortem.
Jess: quick troubleshooting snippet for logs if needed: ```
# find workers with high kv
kubectl logs -l app=inference-runtime -c runtime --since=1h | grep "kv_size_bytes" | sort -r
# apply override for single node
curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" https://ops-api.internal/flags -d '{"node":"node-abc","kernel.select_override":"prefer_fp16"}'
```
Arjun: note to devs — sample delta for KV per-token observed in profiling: gptq=120B/token, awq=330B/token for Llama-3-70B layers 6–12. We should treat >200B/token as a red flag.
Priya: thanks team. Final summary before handoff: paused AWQ rollout, applied kernel override + aggressive eviction, reduced batching, staged capacity bump, customers notified, postmortem scheduled. Running metrics look stable. Marc takes over.
Marc: thanks — taking over. I'll keep thread updated with any regressions or additional customer impact. If we need an urgent rollback of model changes, I'll coordinate with model-onboarding.
Priya: I’ll file the incident and add required runbook updates. Good triage — great work. :thumbsup:
